newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds post positive returns.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds post positive returns.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds posted an average return of 1.2 percent in October, thanks to a strong performance by the bond market, Meitav Investments and Securities said in its monthly report on Sunday.
In spite of the rise, the index of 308 mutual funds was down 0.2 percent for the first 10 months of the year, reflecting the downturn in share prices.

The index of bond funds rose 1.8 percent in October, bringing the rise for the first 10 months to 6.9 percent. The bond market marked its second higher month in a row, due to lower levels of redemptions in the provident funds, which reduced selling presure on bonds, and expectations of increased Treasury borrowing, Meitav said.
Bond prices fell sharply in July and August under pressure from high interest rates and massive public redemptions in the provident funds.

Equity funds continued to do poorly, with the equity fund index falling 0.3 percent for the month and 15.2 percent for the year to date. Meitav said shares fell in the month because of tensions with neighbouring Syria, troubles in negotiations with the Palestinians and a slowing economy.
